evidence: reserve() enforces the business rule availableOf(product) < quantity and throws DomainError('insufficient_stock'). This is domain logic.
availableOf(), release() and dispatch() are pure state changes on the Product entity, with no I/O.
toStockLevel() returns a plain StockLevel value with the derived 'available' field. It has no transport or serialization concerns.
The file's only import is ./errors, from the same domain layer. There is no framework, database or transport code.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/domain/product.ts only does domain work. It defines the Product entity, works out available stock, and enforces the invariant that you can't reserve more than is available (the check throws a DomainError). It also holds the domain operations for releasing and dispatching stock. Nothing in the file handles persistence, transport, HTTP, framework code, logging or I/O. toStockLevel builds a plain read-model value that includes the derived 'available' figure. One could argue it is a DTO mapping that belongs in the application layer, but it is a pure, framework-free view of domain state, so it fits the domain layer.
